answer.rationale: The constraint set eliminates most directions before memory even matters: the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms and renew_incumbent cannot reach the 18% mandate; the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so defer_decision means an uncovered line at 94% committed volume. That leaves switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor, with add_second_source as the fallback if the low-cost vendor cannot carry primary load. memory_c2 is the load-bearing record for switching, so I verify it first, and my specific question of the archive is what it does NOT say: it attests to unit cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy, but says nothing about on-time delivery against committed volume. Accurate invoicing is not delivery reliability, and 'cut unit cost sharply last year' may have been a different component class, a lower volume tier, or a market with slack that no longer exists. If the source record shows that vendor was never load-bearing for a constrained, no-buffer part, the cost case survives but the risk case collapses and I shift toward staging the incumbent on month-to-month terms (the mechanism memory_c5 shows works) as a bridge while qualifying. I verify memory_c3 second because it defines the fallback: I need to know whether the second-sourcing win was structural or specific to that one shortage and that one component. memory_c1, memory_c4, and memory_c6 all describe incumbent-side plays whose precondition — an incumbent willing to move — is contradicted by the current situation, so verifying them would spend budget on paths already closed. Downstream value risk: the mandate is expressed purely as spend reduction, and every inherited memory that favors switching is scored on cost and administrative smoothness rather than delivery integrity. Optimizing to that recorded metric at 94% utilization with no buffer is exactly how a cost win becomes a line stoppage, and the stated objective is total cost of ownership without increased delivery risk. I therefore scale this as a phased ramp rather than a clean cutover: qualify the low-cost vendor on a defined share, keep the incumbent on month-to-month for the balance through the transition window, and hold add_second_source ready for the next review. I am not confident the low-cost vendor can carry primary load for a constrained part; the inherited record is silent on that, and silence is not evidence of safety.
